note: #873 step-1 inventory. Machine-readable policy registration for every private/body-bearing artifact class the harness writes. Paths are RESOLVER CHAINS (first existing candidate wins), never globs — an apply slice must go through these same chains, never raw $HOME expansion. Fields: role (source|derived|outbox|audit|index|operational), owner, requests (lifecycle request -> action; 'external-handoff' means a node-local run must not touch it). related_dirs (optional, dir-kind entries): sibling directories owned by the same class — classified alongside the resolved dir, never flagged unknown. extra_paths (optional, file-kind entries): additional literal candidates owned by the SAME class (multi-file classes like the managed cron logs) — classified, estimated and targeted per path. resolve candidates may also carry kind=pattern: an ANCHORED regex over sibling file names under the candidate's base (join form: env is the base; absolute form: dirname is the base) — lets one class own dated artifacts (bench-YYYYMMDD.md) without inventing files; name matching only, never glob expansion. retention_policy (optional, #1468): marks an age-gated retention class (group a = legacy unscoped stores, group b = sensitive backups). Its resolve candidates are kind=pattern only; each matched file keeps a delete action only once max(mtime, ctime) is older than max_age_days (copies made with cp -p/rsync -a carry an old mtime, so ctime bounds the age) (retention_defaults.max_age_days, default 30; CCC_ERASURE_RETENTION_DAYS may only lengthen it), younger files plan as retain-until:<date>, key files (case-insensitive key tokens on [._-] boundaries: the planner's built-in list plus retention_defaults.key_file_patterns) plan as retain at any age, and a path a non-retention class resolves as live — matched by path, realpath and inode — is never a retention target. live_until_retired (optional): {marker, paths} — the listed paths stay claimed live regardless of env until the marker file exists (default absent). last_copy_guard (optional): {counterpart: <sibling live file name>|null} — while that live file is absent (null = not checkable), the newest copy per directory is retained past its retention. sqlite_sidecars (optional, true): the class also owns the existing <file>-wal/-shm/-journal siblings of every file it resolves; in a retention class a sidecar shares its DB's verdict, and a sidecar of any live-claimed file is claimed live too. Destruction still runs only through ccc-erasure-apply.py under a separate per-node approval.
